Recognizing the immediate threat, Umbrasa bio-engineers developed innovative **Helio-Regulators**—symbiotic wearable mantles interwoven with specialized helium-producing fungi. These organisms efficiently filtered and converted atmospheric gases, producing a breathable, helium-rich microenvironment, enabling the Umbrasa to safely inhabit Primus’s surface. Despite the ingenuity of this biotechnology, periodic replenishment of helium remained a necessity, encouraging careful management of resources and meticulous planning of surface operations.

Upon initial landings, the Umbrasa established peaceful contact with various terrestrial societies, who regarded them with fascination and cautious optimism. Their unique appearances—compact stature, armored bodies, glowing breaths, and finely-tuned ears—intrigued native Primus races, inspiring curiosity and admiration. Quickly integrating into the local cultures, the Umbrasa shared their distinctive knowledge of gravitational manipulation and neon-based artistic performances, rapidly becoming esteemed contributors to Primus’s diverse civilizations.

The Umbrasa found particularly welcoming communities among mountain-dwelling societies, such as those inhabiting floating islands and cliff-side settlements, whose cultures shared a natural affinity for heights, gravity, and precision architecture. Here, Umbrasa gravity-balanced structures—bridges seemingly suspended in mid-air and gravity-defying amphitheaters—captivated locals, who eagerly adopted these innovative construction techniques.

Perhaps most beloved were the Umbrasa’s cultural performances. Using carefully timed exhalations during atmospheric electrical disturbances, skilled Umbrasa performers illuminated their neon breath in vibrant displays, creating mesmerizing, ephemeral images that conveyed stories of their origins, struggles, and triumphs. Their helium-infused speech, characterized by melodic tonalities, earned them affectionate nicknames among terrestrial communities, such as the “Laughing Shadows,” further deepening cultural bonds.

Despite their successful integration, the return to Primus was emotionally complex. Many Umbrasa families, descendants of miners whose loved ones had been left behind on Earth during the Undertow, searched eagerly for ancestral connections, only to discover scarce clues and faded memories. This longing to reconnect with lost lineages became central to their personal and cultural narratives, adding layers of melancholy and hope to their collective experience.

Thus, their return marked both a reunion with ancestral dreams and the forging of new bonds, establishing the Umbrasa as respected architects, revered storytellers, and skilled diplomats, seamlessly blending their lunar heritage into the rich tapestry of Primus’s civilizations.

record.title: Helio-Regulator mantles
record.summary: Fungal mantles that make helium, so the Umbrasa can live in the world's air.

record.title: Echocrafters
record.summary: Resonara who shape waves into constructs, summoned beings and armour.
record.body:
For a select few Resonara, the Divergence granted the power to manipulate waves on an **advanced level**, turning their illusions into something far more **tangible**. These Resonara became known as **Echocrafters**, individuals who could **create physical constructs** from waves, giving **solid form** to the things they imagined.

- **Physical Illusions**: While most Resonara could only create **non-physical illusions**, Echocrafters could give these illusions **physical form**, transforming light, sound, and resonance into **solid constructs**. These constructs could be used as **weapons**, **tools**, or even **creatures** in battle.

- **Summoning Beasts and Constructs**: The most advanced Echocrafters were able to go beyond simple illusions, becoming **summoners** in a sense. They could use their powers to create **creatures or beings** from pure resonance, which could act as temporary **companions** in battle or serve them in other ways. These summoned creatures were not independent, but rather extensions of the Echocrafters’ will, tethered to their powers and able to fight alongside them for a limited time.

- **Resonant Armor and Shields**: Some Echocrafters could also summon **armor or shields** made from resonant waves, creating protective barriers that could deflect attacks and absorb damage. This ability made them formidable defenders on the battlefield, as they could summon these barriers almost instantly.

While these powers made the **Echocrafters** respected and feared, their ability to **manifest waves into tangible forms** was not without limits. Summoning too many constructs at once could weaken them, and maintaining these creations for long periods drained their energy. Nonetheless, their summoning abilities elevated them to a status of **elite warriors and protectors**, especially within the nomadic Troupes.

record.title: Sons of the Sirens
record.summary: Destructive Resonara mercenaries.
record.body:
Among the Echocrafters, a darker group emerged known as the **Sons of the Sirens**—Resonara who used their advanced powers for **chaos and destruction**. These individuals were not healers or artists, but **mercenaries**, hired to **disrupt and destabilize** in combat. While the Echocrafters were known for creating constructs and companions, the **Sons of the Sirens** specialized in using their abilities to **disorient** and **destroy**.

- **Sonic Disruption**: The Sons of the Sirens could **amplify sound waves**, creating overwhelming **sonic blasts** that shattered structures or incapacitated enemies through sheer sensory overload.

- **Wave Distortion**: They could twist **sound and light** to create **chaos on the battlefield**, making it difficult for enemies to orient themselves. They used their powers to disorient entire armies, creating blind spots or false terrain to confuse and mislead.

- **Summoning Beasts of Destruction**: Like other Echocrafters, the Sons of the Sirens could summon **creatures** made from resonance. However, their summoned beasts were designed for **destruction** rather than defense, taking the form of **ferocious monsters** that rampaged through enemy lines, spreading chaos and fear.

The **Sons of the Sirens** became notorious for their ruthless tactics, leaving a trail of **discord and destruction** in their wake. Hired by warlords and factions seeking to disrupt their enemies, they were feared across the world as **bringers of chaos**, their powers a twisted reflection of the harmonious art their people had once valued. Though the Resonara viewed them with **wariness** or outright disdain, the Sons of the Sirens were a reminder of how the Divergence had not only granted their people new powers but had also unleashed darker forces among them.

record.title: The Song of Unmaking
record.summary: Where a weapons project had thinned the walls of the world, the Undertow sang.
record.body:
The **Song of Unmaking** was not a sound as mortals typically understand it. It was a resonance that echoed across **dimensional planes**, so powerful that it pierced the very fabric of existence. When it struck the land, it did not simply pass through the people; it **rewrote them**, resonating deep within their bodies and unraveling their DNA. The sound was overwhelming—those affected could not stand under its weight. Every living being, from bustling cities to rural hamlets, collapsed as the **Song** shattered their human forms and began the long process of reweaving them into something else entirely.

Though the outside world experienced chaotic natural disasters, this region was overtaken by a far stranger transformation. The people fell to the ground as one, frozen in a stasis that would last for years. The **Song of Unmaking** was more than a moment of devastation—it was a dimensional force that initiated the **Silence of Becoming**, a period of total stillness where the Resonara’s bodies were **reformed** by the resonances that had flooded their land.

record.title: Windows of Memory
record.summary: Brief rifts that show the Resonara the past and the future.
record.body:
As the **Age of the Abyssal Veil** progressed, the **dimensional membrane** around the Resonara’s homeland remained **thin**, a lingering effect of the disruptions caused by **Project Zorya** and the **Undertow**. Over time, the strange phenomena they had first noticed—like the **ghost sounds** and **flickers of light**—began to evolve. What had once been faint disturbances at the edges of their perception grew into something far more significant: the **Windows of Memory**.

These **windows** were brief, shimmering rifts that would appear in the air, revealing **glimpses into other times**—both the **distant past** and **possible futures**. Through these windows, the Resonara could witness **fragments of ancient civilizations**, long-lost cultures, and future worlds yet to unfold. While the images they saw were fleeting and often difficult to interpret, they were undeniably **beautiful** and full of **artistic wonder**. The Resonara were captivated by the elegance of these visions, and although they couldn’t fully understand the cultures or events they witnessed, they found deep meaning in the **art** and **beauty** of what they saw.

These glimpses into other times became a profound source of inspiration for the Resonara, leading them to create **grand epics**, elaborate **plays**, and powerful **symphonies** that captured the essence of the **Windows of Memory**. Their art told the stories of the worlds they had glimpsed, combining what they saw with their own interpretations and emotions. These **performances** became central to Resonara culture, offering a way to share the mystery and wonder of the **windows** with each other and the world.

However, the rest of the world met these tales with **skepticism**. Outsiders could not see the **Windows of Memory** and doubted the **authenticity** of the Resonara’s stories. To those beyond their borders, the idea that the Resonara could witness glimpses of the **past and future** seemed far-fetched. This skepticism was further fueled by the fact that the Resonara lived in a **lush, untouched paradise**, spared from the devastation that had ravaged the rest of the world during the **Undertow**. Many outsiders felt **resentment** toward the Resonara, viewing them as **privileged** and **out of touch** with the struggles of other societies.

Despite this, the Resonara continued to create their epic **performances**, determined to preserve the beauty and mystery of the **Windows of Memory**, even if others refused to believe them.

record.title: The Echoing Miasma
record.summary: A dark fog that swallows sound and light; the Resonara's Drowning.
record.body:
The **Drowning** marked the end of the Resonara’s lush, paradise-like homeland. When the Tide struck, it unleashed a creeping force known as the **Echoing Miasma**—a thick, dark fog that suffocated the life and resonance of the Resonara’s land. The Echoing Miasma wasn’t just an ordinary fog; it swallowed sound, light, and the very waves that the Resonara had once used to perceive the world. It warped the harmony of the land, replacing it with a dull, choking dissonance.

The **Echoing Miasma** turned their once-vibrant landscape into a twisted shadow of its former self. **Plants withered**, the air grew heavy and oppressive, and the Resonara’s ability to sense the world through **waves** was dulled and distorted. The resonance that had once shaped their lives was now replaced by a disorienting, suffocating **silence** that filled them with dread. The dissonant hum of the Miasma reverberated through the land, choking their homeland and leaving them with no choice but to **flee**.

Faced with the overwhelming spread of the Echoing Miasma, the Resonara were forced into a **mass exodus**, abandoning their once-idyllic paradise. They fled into the outside world, not as explorers but as **refugees**, seeking shelter and integration into new societies. They left in large, organized groups called **Troupes**, which became the heart of Resonara society in exile.

The **Troupes** served different purposes, depending on the talents and goals of their members:

- Some Troupes became **traveling performers**, using their musical and artistic skills to earn their way in new lands. They put on **elaborate shows**, weaving sound, light, and waves into immersive performances that captivated audiences across the world.

- Other Troupes took on the role of **healers**, using their subtle wave manipulation abilities to treat the **mind and spirit**. While other cultures focused on physical healing, the Resonara healers were renowned for their ability to soothe mental trauma, grief, and emotional scars left in the wake of the Tide.

- Still, others integrated into the societies they encountered, offering their abilities in return for shelter and resources.

The Resonara, once proud of their **paradise**, now wandered the world as **displaced refugees**, known for their talents but burdened by the loss of their homeland.

record.title: The Normandy Enclave
record.summary: Soldiers of both sides of a beach landing, pulled through a rift on a moonlit night; now one wary town of salvage and steel.
record.body:
## About

The Normandy Enclave, nestled on the sandy shores of this enigmatic futuristic planet, stands as a testament to the convergence of past and future, where echoes of history collide with the innovations of tomorrow.

Stretching along the coastline, this enclave is a patchwork of salvaged relics from a bygone era and sleek, futuristic architecture, forming a unique blend of nostalgia and progress. The landscape is dotted with the remnants of once-mighty war machines—beached aircraft carriers now repurposed into bustling hubs of activity, their rusted hulls serving as a reminder of the tumultuous events that led to their arrival.

Narrow cobblestone streets wind their way through the settlement, lined with a hodgepodge of structures fashioned from salvaged materials and advanced alloys. The air is thick with the scent of saltwater and industry, mingling with the sounds of bustling markets and the hum of machinery.

At the heart of the enclave lies a central square, where a weathered monument stands as a tribute to those who arrived during the tumult of The Tide. Flags of different nations flutter in the breeze, a symbol of unity forged amidst chaos.

Despite the challenges posed by their new reality, the inhabitants of the Normandy Enclave are a resilient lot, bound together by a shared history and a determination to carve out a future in this unfamiliar world. Within the enclave's walls, a sense of camaraderie thrives, as individuals from disparate backgrounds come together to build a community that honors the past while embracing the possibilities of the future.

## History

In the wake of The Tide, as Primus staggered to comprehend the breadth of its upheaval, one of the most intriguing Enclaves emerged: The Normandy Enclave.

It was a cool, moonlit night when the echoes of gunfire and the thunderous roar of engines disrupted the serenity of a quiet shoreline. Along the coast, where the waves lapped against the sand with rhythmic persistence, a rift in space-time tore open, unleashing a torrent of chaos and confusion onto the once tranquil beach. Soldiers, weary and disoriented, stumbled through the rift, their uniforms tattered and their faces etched with shock and disbelief.

These were the brave souls of the Battle of Normandy, plucked from the annals of history and thrust into the bewildering embrace of a world they could scarcely comprehend. Among them were American GIs and German Wehrmacht soldiers, their enmity momentarily forgotten in the face of this new and incomprehensible reality.

As they gathered on the shore, surrounded by the remnants of their shattered past, they found themselves confronted not only by the unfamiliar landscape of Primus but also by the myriad dangers that lurked within it. Strange creatures, born of The Tide's transformative energies, prowled the shadows, their eyes glinting with predatory hunger. For the soldiers of Normandy, survival became their immediate and singular focus, as they struggled to make sense of their newfound existence in a world teetering on the brink of chaos.

In the days that followed, the Normandy Enclave took shape amidst the wreckage of their former lives. Drawing upon the skills and camaraderie forged in the crucible of war, the inhabitants of this makeshift settlement banded together, determined to carve out a place for themselves in this alien landscape.

Led by a council of former officers, both American and German, the Normandy Enclave became a bastion of unity and resilience in a world torn asunder by The Tide's merciless embrace. Through grit and determination, they transformed the shattered remnants of their past into a beacon of hope amidst the chaos, offering shelter and solace to all who sought refuge within their walls.

Yet, even as they sought to rebuild their lives, the specter of their shared history loomed large, casting a shadow of doubt and mistrust over their fragile community. Old rivalries and prejudices simmered beneath the surface, threatening to tear apart the fragile bonds that held them together.

But despite the challenges they faced, the people of the Normandy Enclave refused to surrender to despair. United by their shared struggle and fueled by the hope of a brighter tomorrow, they stood as a testament to the indomitable spirit of humanity, defiant in the face of adversity.

And so, as the moon rose high above the shores of Primus, casting its silver light upon the world below, the Normandy Enclave endured, a beacon of resilience amidst the tumultuous sea of uncertainty that surrounded them. In the heart of this new world, where the echoes of the past mingled with the promise of the future, they stood as living testament to the enduring power of the human spirit.

record.title: The Conquistador Brotherhood
record.summary: An enclave out of the Drift, hunted by the Geomagnus and hidden by those who pity them.
record.body:
When the **Drift** fractured the boundaries between dimensions, pulling enclaves from Earth’s history into the world of Primus, the **Conquistador Brotherhood** found themselves in an unfamiliar and hostile world. The once-feared Conquistadors, with their **iron armor**, **muskets**, and **swords**, were completely outmatched by the advanced powers of the **Geomagnus**, the authoritarian elite of the Obscarron. What had once made the Conquistadors mighty—steel weapons and colonial tactics—was now **obsolete** against the **magnetic** and **geothermal** powers wielded by the Obscarron.

The **Obscarron**, unaware of the Conquistadors’ history as conquerors and colonizers, viewed these strange armored invaders with disdain and disgust. The **Geomagnus** saw them as an **inferior plague**—primitive creatures who had no place in their advanced society, and whose presence threatened the balance of the core. Thus, the **Geomagnus** declared the Conquistadors as **vermin to be exterminated**.

What followed was a brutal campaign known as **The Cull**.

record.title: Arrival
record.summary: Breathe, little spark. An introduction for those who wash ashore.
record.body:
> Waves crash upon shores,  
> As the Tide's eternal song,  
> Echoes through the void.

Breathe, little spark, adrift upon currents far from your origin. Yes, the disorientation… it clings like sea mist. You have washed upon the shores of **Primus**, a world that likely feels fundamentally wrong to your senses, yet strangely… resonant. Do not fight the confusion; it is the nature of arrival here, a passage through the unseen eddies that churn between realities. You are here now, and the now of Primus is a thing woven from echoes and storms.

Look beyond your immediate footing. See how the light falls differently here, perhaps? How shadows seem deeper, holding whispers your ears almost catch? Feel the very air, thick with energies that vibrate just beneath perception? This is Primus as it is, a realm sculpted by forces that disregard the neat lines of cause and effect your own time might have known. Civilizations rise here not just on solid ground, but amongst impossible **Floating Mountains** that drift on unseen currents. Forests pulse with unsettling bio-luminescence, deserts howl with storms that taste of ozone and something other, and the deep oceans cradle secrets far older and stranger than the surface dwellers comprehend.

The peoples you encounter – the Primal races – they reflect this fractured beauty. They are beings born of adaptation, their forms often merging flesh with stone, light with shadow, mechanism with life. They wield powers that might seem like magic to you – bending gravity, whispering to time, shaping matter with focused will, touching minds across vast distances. Do not mistake this for mere chaos; it is the intricate harmony of survival in a world where the fundamental laws have been… re-tuned. They live amidst ruins that sing forgotten histories and build cities that hum with energies drawn from the planet's altered heart. They remember little of the world before the great changes, their pasts often as fragmented and dreamlike as your own sudden arrival.

What force sculpted such a reality? What power underpins this constant state of flux, this blending of the mundane and the miraculous? It is the deep, pervasive rhythm the inhabitants name **"The Tide."** Think of it not as a singular catastrophe that struck and faded, but as the enduring ocean upon which this reality floats. It is the underlying song, the cosmic breath that dictates the ebb and flow of possibility here. The Tide washed through existence across vast cycles, thinning the veils, allowing the profound and the perilous to intermingle, leaving behind its indelible signature in **Three Consequences** that define every aspect of life on Primus. Listen, and perhaps you will begin to understand the verses of this eternal song…

The **first consequence**, felt as a tremor in the very bones of the planet, was **"The Drowning."** The physical laws seemed to sigh and shift. Lands convulsed, coastlines vanished under hungry waters, mountains shattered, some plunging into fiery oblivion, others torn loose to hang suspended in the troubled sky – islands adrift on currents of altered gravity. Cities built across millennia vanished overnight, leaving behind ghostly ruins or gaping maws in the earth. Where connection once thrived, fragmentation bloomed. From this reshaping, survivors clung to islands of stability – some sealed in desperate isolation, others reaching out, becoming fragile harbors for the displaced, all forever marked by the memory of solid ground yielding beneath them, forever navigating the turbulent waters of this new age.

The **second consequence**, **"The Divergence,"** resonated within the survivors themselves, an awakening of potentials long dormant or perhaps entirely new. The fundamental forces of the universe seemed to offer themselves to those who could perceive their altered harmony. Gravity yielded its secrets, granting flight or crushing weight. Time frayed at the edges, becoming a weapon or a shield for those attuned to its flow. Matter itself grew mutable, responsive to focused will, enabling acts of creation or healing once deemed impossible. The unseen threads connecting minds allowed passage across space or the brief summoning of echoes. Light, heat, the very essence of energy answered new masters. These abilities, wondrous and terrifying, are now woven into the fabric of Primus, seeding conflict and innovation alike. Wonder and peril became intimate companions.

The **third consequence**, **"The Drift,"** is the chaotic tide that likely carried you here. Spacetime itself frayed, opening **"Drifts"** – shimmering anomalies, gateways through which fragments of other realities, other timelines, wash ashore onto Primus. Entire populations, relics of forgotten epochs, shards of worlds utterly alien arrive unbidden, forming fragile **"Enclaves."** These pockets of the displaced struggle for existence, facing monstrous creatures born of The Tide, the suspicion of Primus's natives, and the echoes of their own severed histories. They stand now as living paradoxes, constant reminders that the boundaries of reality here are… porous, forever shifting.

So you stand now upon Primus, a world breathing the aftermath and the ongoing resonance of The Tide. The rules you knew are memories carried on the wind. Here, science and myth dance together in the deep currents. Survival is fluidity, resilience is attunement. The past is not gone, merely displaced, drifting alongside a present teeming with volatile potential.

Feel the vibrations beneath your feet. Listen beyond the sounds you recognize. Your arrival is another ripple, another note added to the endless song. Observe, adapt, and perhaps find your own place within this profound, perilous harmony. And so, our story begins…

record.title: The Undertow, the Age of the Veil and the Tide
record.summary: Settled by Tide 101: the Undertow (~2102 B.U.), then the Age of the Veil (~700 years), then the Era of Verdancy, within which the Tide occurs.

record.title: How long was the Age of the Veil?
record.summary: Tide 101 says about 700 years; the Umbrasa document about 900; the Resonara document “thousands of years”.

record.title: The Petrification and the Geomagnus
record.summary: The Obscarron document: floods hardened the lava rivers and the Geomagnus rose in the Divergence. The Teruānga document: a creeping calcification, with the Geomagnus rising because of it, and a Nagga Kai invasion of flooded Obscarron lands that the Obscarron document never mentions (it also says they lived far from the oceans).

record.title: Two drafts of the Nyth'rok today
record.summary: The Nyth'rok document has two Drift sections and two “today” sections that disagree (the Nyth'vael dominant across the world vs dwindling in the Stillholds), and gives time powers to different factions in different places.

record.title: The Umbrasa's Three Consequences
record.summary: The Umbrasa document ties the Three Consequences to the Undertow and describes the Drowning as gravitational fracturing on the moon, unlike the other documents.

record.title: Aircraft carriers at Normandy
record.summary: The enclave's beached aircraft carriers were not part of the landings; perhaps landing craft or battleships, or something the Drift brought from another time.

record.title: Operation or Project Zorya
record.summary: The Resonara document uses both names for the weapons project behind the Song of Unmaking.

record.title: Irridosai or Irridosa
record.summary: Tide 101 says Irridosai; the Teruānga document says Irridosa (and mentions their Aetherfallen).
